title: How To Stop Your Class From Calling Out
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin lays out a nine-step process for breaking a class's habit of calling out without raising their hand once it has taken hold. Key steps include reteaching the hand-raising rule from scratch, having the teacher take responsibility for the lapse rather than blaming students, explaining why the rule matters, physically demonstrating correct behavior, promising to enforce consistently going forward, and using deliberate pauses—both before responding to a raised hand and when a wave of call-outs first tests the reset rule. He also addresses individual repeat offenders with a more measured, low-key correction. He closes by noting teachers can deliberately suspend the rule for defined discussion periods, as long as the parameters and expectations for polite participation are made explicit beforehand.
points: Lays out a nine-step process for resetting a class that has slipped into habitually calling out without raising hands.
Recommends the teacher take responsibility for the lapse rather than blaming or lecturing students.
Advises physically demonstrating correct hand-raising and waiting behavior rather than just describing it.
Introduces the 'long pause'—stopping everything and waiting silently when a class first tests a newly reset rule.
Notes teachers can deliberately suspend the hand-raising rule for defined discussion periods if expectations are set explicitly beforehand.
quotes: Before you know it, so many students are calling out without raising their hand that it becomes impossible to enforce.
Instead of lecturing or blaming your students for the disruptions, take responsibility yourself. Let them know that you haven’t done a good job protecting their right to learn.
Although it may seem silly or unnecessary, show your students exactly what raising their hand and waiting patiently to be called on looks like. It’s best to sit at a student’s desk.
Chances are, at least for a day or so, you’ll be tested. When it happens, and your students start calling out one after the other, stop everything. Just stand and wait. Take a long pause.
Another powerful strategy to break the habit of calling out is to never call on a student the moment their hand goes up. Pause first, disrupt the ‘teacher-looks-I-answer’ rhythm, then call on them.
Following the nine steps above, and being clear about when the rule isn’t in play, will remove calling out from your classroom.
